ANT GAR - Inpatient Cardiology Progress Note
Salient Cardiac Features


Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure with bilateral lower extremity DVTs and persistent high clinical suspicion for pulmonary embolism as the primary etiology.


Heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction demonstrating excellent response to aggressive diuresis with approximately 12-pound weight loss.


Morbid obesity and obstructive sleep apnea requiring long-term risk factor modification and outpatient management.


SOAP Note
Subjective


The patient reports continued improvement in breathing and overall feels better.


Denies new chest pain or other acute cardiac complaints.


Discussed that the overall clinical picture is increasingly suggestive of pulmonary embolism given persistent exertional tachycardia, bilateral DVTs, and elevated D-dimer despite concurrent heart failure.


Congratulated the patient on his significant weight loss efforts and encouraged continued lifestyle modification. The importance of treating obstructive sleep apnea to improve long-term cardiovascular health was also discussed.


Objective
Vitals reviewed elsewhere.
General: Awake, alert, no acute distress.
Cardiovascular: Tachycardic with exertion but hemodynamically stable.
Respiratory: Oxygen requirement has improved from approximately 6 L/min to 4 L/min. No clinical evidence of bacterial pneumonia.
Extremities: Significant improvement in volume status following aggressive diuresis.
Laboratory data reviewed. Echocardiogram reviewed. Bilateral lower extremity DVTs and elevated D-dimer remain highly concerning for pulmonary embolism.
Assessment


Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure with bilateral lower extremity DVTs and high clinical suspicion for pulmonary embolism. (ICD-10: J96.01, I82.403)


Acute on chronic heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction, markedly improved following aggressive diuresis. (ICD-10: I50.22)


Elevated troponin consistent with demand ischemia/right ventricular strain. (ICD-10: R79.89)


Morbid obesity with obstructive sleep apnea. (ICD-10: E66.01, G47.33)


No convincing evidence of bacterial pneumonia. (ICD-10: J18.9 excluded clinically)


Plan


Continue therapeutic anticoagulation.


Transition Bumex infusion to furosemide 40 mg PO twice daily.


Continue spironolactone 25 mg PO twice daily.


Continue gradual oxygen weaning as tolerated.


Continue evaluation and treatment for suspected pulmonary embolism.


Continue weight-loss efforts and reinforce treatment of obstructive sleep apnea.


Discharge once oxygen requirements improve sufficiently for safe outpatient management.


High-complexity medical decision-making performed due to acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, suspected pulmonary embolism with bilateral DVTs, heart failure management, diuretic transition, oxygen titration, and anticoagulation management.


Nursing Communication


Continue therapeutic anticoagulation per protocol.


Discontinue Bumex infusion.


Start furosemide 40 mg PO twice daily.


Start spironolactone 25 mg PO twice daily.


Perform a supervised 6-minute room air oxygen challenge. If oxygen saturation falls below 87%, immediately resume supplemental oxygen and titrate to maintain oxygen saturation approximately 90-91%.


Tiger Text cardiology with the lowest room air oxygen saturation achieved and the duration of the room air trial.


Continue strict intake/output and daily weights.


Notify cardiology for worsening hypoxemia, chest pain, hypotension, increasing tachycardia, or other clinical deterioration.
